definitions.explanation: A formal, collective term for rivers and streams. Used primarily in official, administrative, scientific, and news contexts rather than everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: {河川|かせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{水位|すいい}→水位：21569_suii⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上昇|じょうしょう}している→上昇する：21681_joushousuru⟧。
examples.english: The river's water level is rising.

examples.japanese: {河川|かせん}{敷|じき}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦バーベキュー→バーベキュー：27519_baabekyuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: More people are having barbecues on the riverbank.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大雨|おおあめ}→大雨：03015_ooame⟧⟦による→による：28349_niyoru⟧{河川|かせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{氾濫|はんらん}→氾濫：09256_hanran⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}ぐ→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧、⟦{堤防|ていぼう}→堤防：19409_teibou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{整備|せいび}→整備：04037_seibi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{急|いそ}がれている→急ぐ：01191_isogu⟧。
examples.english: Improvements to embankments are being expedited to prevent river flooding due to heavy rain.

notes:
USAGE:
{河川|かせん} is the formal/administrative term for rivers. In everyday speech, ⟦{川|かわ}→川：02186_kawa⟧ (river) is used. {河川|かせん} appears in news, government documents, and technical contexts. The compound combines {河|か} (large river) and {川|せん} (river/stream), so it covers waterways of all sizes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {河川|かせん}{敷|じき}: riverbed, riverside open space
- {河川|かせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{氾濫|はんらん}→氾濫：09256_hanran⟧: river flooding
- {河川|かせん}⟦{管理|かんり}→管理：00178_kanri⟧: river management
- {河川|かせん}⟦{工事|こうじ}→工事：00244_kouji⟧: river construction/maintenance work
- {一級|いっきゅう}{河川|かせん}: class-1 river (managed by national government)
